title: Rooms in the house
scope: Postpositions में, पर, तक, को, से; the oblique case of nouns, adjectives and pronouns; possessives मेरा, तुम्हारा, आपका; “there is” word order and कहाँ

vocab.en: oblique singular of कौन and क्या
oblique plural of कौन and क्या

items.q: Fill the gap: “The books are in the cupboard.”
items.en: The books[0] are[3] in[2] the cupboard[1].
wrong: पर means “on” a surface, or “at” a place or time (घर पर “at home”, समय पर “on time”).
items.why: Inside a cupboard is में. Like every postposition, it follows its noun: अलमारी में.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The newspaper is on the bed.”
items.en: The newspaper[0] is[3] on[2] the bed[1].
wrong: में would put the newspaper inside the bed. On a surface is पर.
तक means “up to, as far as, until”.
items.why: On a surface is पर, placed after the noun.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where are you from?”
items.en: Where[1] are[3] you[0] from[2]?
wrong: कहाँ में is not said. “From where” is कहाँ से.
कहाँ तक asks “how far?”, not “where from?”.
items.why: “From” is से, so आप कहाँ से हैं ? asks where someone comes from.

items.q: Fill the gap: “I am from London.”
items.en: I[0] am[3] from[2] London[1].
wrong: मैं लंदन में हूँ would mean “I am in London”.
पर means “on” a surface, or “at” a place or time (घर पर “at home”, समय पर “on time”).
items.why: Where someone comes from takes से.

items.q: Fill the gap: “She is in Delhi until Monday.”
items.say: वह सोमवार तक दिल्ली में है ।
items.en: She[0] is[5] in[4] Delhi[3] until[2] Monday[1].
wrong: सोमवार से would mean “since Monday”, the opposite end of the time.
को means “to”, and with a few time words “at” (रात को “at night”). “Until” is तक.
items.why: “Until” is तक, after the time word.

items.q: Fill the gap: “At night the garden is very beautiful.”
items.say: रात को बग़ीचा बहुत सुन्दर है ।
items.en: At[1] night[0] the garden[2] is[5] very[3] beautiful[4].
wrong: रात से would mean “since last night”.
items.why: रात को is the set phrase for “at night”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Grandmother has been ill since the morning.”
items.say: दादी जी सुबह से बीमार हैं ।
items.en: Grandmother[0] {has been}[5] ill[4] since[3] the morning[2].
wrong: सुबह तक would mean “until the morning”.
को means “to”, and with a few time words “at” (रात को “at night”). “Since” is से.
items.why: “Since” a time is से. Hindi uses the present tense for a state that has lasted since then.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The bird is on the stone.”
items.en: The bird[0] is[3] on[2] the stone[1].
wrong: में would put the bird inside the stone. On top of it is पर.
items.why: On a surface is पर.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What is in the drawer?”
items.en: What[2] is[3] in[1] the drawer[0]?
wrong: दराज़ पर would be “on the drawer”, on top of it.
को means “to”, and with a few time words “at” (रात को “at night”).
items.why: Inside something is में.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Everything is clean from here to there.”
items.hi: यहाँ ___ वहाँ तक सब साफ़ है ।
items.say: यहाँ से वहाँ तक सब साफ़ है ।
items.en: Everything[4] is[6] clean[5] from[1] here[0] to[3] there[2].
wrong: यहाँ में is not said. The starting point is यहाँ से.
को marks “to”, but the starting point of a stretch is से.
items.why: से … तक is “from … to, as far as”.

lessons.title: Nouns before postpositions
lessons.desc: The oblique case, singular and plural

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are two beds in the room.”
items.en: There are[4] two[2] beds[3] in[1] the room[0].
wrong: कमरा is the direct form. In front of में the noun is oblique, so -ā becomes -e.
कमरों is the oblique plural, “in the rooms”, but the sentence is about one room.
items.why: Before a postposition a noun is oblique. Masculine nouns in -ā change it to -e in the oblique singular.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children are in the garden.”
items.en: The children[0] are[3] in[2] the garden[1].
wrong: बग़ीचा is the direct form. Before में it must be oblique: बग़ीचे.
बग़ीचों is the oblique plural, “in the gardens”.
items.why: Before a postposition a noun is oblique. Masculine nouns in -ā change it to -e in the oblique singular.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are several children in these houses.”
items.say: इन घरों में कई बच्चे हैं ।
items.en: There are[5] several[3] children[4] in[2] these[0] houses[1].
wrong: घर is the singular (direct or oblique). इन is plural, so the noun must be the oblique plural.
-ẽ is a feminine direct plural ending. घर is masculine, and before में it needs the oblique plural -õ.
items.why: Every noun takes -õ in the oblique plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are books on two tables.”
items.en: There are[4] books[3] on[2] two[0] tables[1].
wrong: मेज़ें is the direct plural. Before पर the oblique plural -õ is needed.
मेज़ is singular, but there are two tables.
items.why: Every noun takes -õ in the oblique plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are several chairs in these rooms.”
items.say: इन कमरों में कई कुरसियाँ हैं ।
items.en: There are[5] several[3] chairs[4] in[2] these[0] rooms[1].
wrong: कमरे before में is the oblique singular, “in the room”. इन is plural, so the oblique plural is needed.
items.why: Every noun takes -õ in the oblique plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Which of those girls is Sangeeta?”
items.say: उन लड़कियों में संगीता कौन है ?
items.en: Which[4] of[2] those[0] girls[1] is[5] Sangeeta[3]?
wrong: लड़कियाँ is the direct plural. Before में the oblique plural is needed.
Before -õ, a final -ī shortens to -iy-: लड़कियों.
items.why: Feminine nouns in -ī take -iyõ in the oblique plural. में here means “among”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are two teachers among these men.”
items.say: इन आदमियों में दो अध्यापक हैं ।
items.en: There are[5] two[3] teachers[4] among[2] these[0] men[1].
wrong: आदमी is the same in the direct singular and plural, but before a postposition the oblique plural is आदमियों.
Before -õ, a final -ī shortens to -iy-: आदमियों.
items.why: Masculine nouns in -ī change to -iy- before the oblique plural -õ.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Father is in the kitchen.”
items.en: Father[0] is[4] in[3] the kitchen[2].
wrong: Only masculine nouns ending in -ā change to -e. रसोईघर does not change in the oblique singular.
रसोईघरों is the oblique plural, “in the kitchens”.
items.why: Masculine nouns that do not end in -ā, and all feminine nouns, look the same in the oblique singular as in the direct.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are new curtains on the doors.”
items.en: There are[4] new[2] curtains[3] on[1] the doors[0].
wrong: दरवाज़े before पर is the oblique singular, “on the door”. The English says doors.
items.why: Every noun takes -õ in the oblique plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “My wife is from this town.”
items.say: मेरी पत्नी इस शहर से है ।
items.en: My[0] wife[1] is[5] from[4] this[2] town[3].
wrong: शहरों is the oblique plural, but इस is singular.
Only masculine nouns ending in -ā change to -e.
items.why: Masculine nouns that do not end in -ā, and all feminine nouns, look the same in the oblique singular as in the direct.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The book is in the drawer.”
items.en: The book[0] is[3] in[2] the drawer[1].
wrong: दराज़ों is the oblique plural, “in the drawers”.
दराज़ें is the direct plural. Feminine nouns do not change in the oblique singular.
items.why: Masculine nouns that do not end in -ā, and all feminine nouns, look the same in the oblique singular as in the direct.

lessons.title: Oblique forms
lessons.desc: Pick the oblique singular or plural of a noun

items.q: Pick the oblique plural of “room” (masculine)
wrong: कमरे is the direct plural and the oblique singular, not the oblique plural.
The final -ā of a masculine noun drops before -õ.
items.why: Masculine nouns in -ā replace it with -õ.

items.q: Pick the oblique plural of “girl” (feminine)
items.why: Nouns in -ī take -iyõ.

items.q: Pick the oblique plural of “man” (masculine)
wrong: आदमी is unchanged in the direct plural, but every noun changes in the oblique plural.
items.why: Nouns in -ī take -iyõ, masculine or feminine.

items.q: Pick the oblique plural of “Hindu” (masculine)
wrong: -iy- is for nouns in -ī. Nouns in -ū just shorten the vowel.
items.why: A final -ū shortens to -u- before the -õ ending.

items.q: Pick the oblique plural of “mother” (feminine)
wrong: Only masculine nouns lose their -ā. Feminine माता keeps it and adds -õ.
items.why: Feminine nouns in -ā keep the -ā and add -õ.

items.q: Pick the oblique plural of “bird” (feminine)
wrong: Nouns in -iyā behave like nouns in -ī and take -iyõ.
items.why: Feminine nouns in -iyā take -iyõ.

items.q: Pick the oblique singular of “garment” (masculine)
wrong: कपड़ा is the direct form. A masculine noun in -ā does not keep it before a postposition.
items.why: Masculine nouns in -ā change it to -e in the oblique singular.

items.q: Pick the oblique singular of “wall” (feminine)
wrong: दीवारें is the direct plural. Feminine nouns do not change in the oblique singular.
items.why: Feminine nouns look the same in the oblique singular as in the direct.

items.q: Pick the oblique singular of “curtain” (masculine)
wrong: Masculine nouns in -ā change in the oblique singular.
items.why: Masculine nouns in -ā change it to -e in the oblique singular.

lessons.title: Adjectives and मेरा, तुम्हारा, आपका
lessons.desc: Adjectives and possessives in the oblique

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are two windows in the big room.”
items.say: बड़े कमरे में दो खिड़कियाँ हैं ।
items.en: There are[5] two[3] windows[4] in[2] the big[0] room[1].
wrong: बड़ा is the direct form. When its noun is oblique, an -ā adjective changes to -e.
बड़ी is feminine, but कमरा is masculine.
items.why: कमरे is oblique before में, so the adjective is oblique too: बड़े.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who is on the black chair?”
items.en: Who[3] is[4] on[2] the black[0] chair[1]?
wrong: -e is the oblique of masculine -ā adjectives. कुरसी is feminine, and -ī never changes.
काला is masculine, but कुरसी is feminine.
items.why: Feminine -ī adjectives stay -ī in the oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are several clothes in my cupboard.”
items.say: मेरी अलमारी में कई कपड़े हैं ।
items.en: There are[5] several[3] clothes[4] in[2] my[0] cupboard[1].
wrong: मेरा agrees with the thing possessed, अलमारी, which is feminine. The -e form is for masculine nouns.
मेरा is masculine, but अलमारी is feminine.
items.why: मेरा agrees like an adjective with the thing possessed.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Is there a garden at your house?”
items.say: क्या आपके घर में बग़ीचा है ?
items.en: Is[5] there a garden[4] at[3] your[1] house[2]?
wrong: आपका is the direct form. घर is oblique before में, so its possessive is too: आपके.
आपकी is feminine, but घर is masculine.
items.why: आपका works like an -ā adjective: -e before an oblique masculine noun.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Grandmother is from a small village.”
items.hi: दादी जी एक ___ गाँव से हैं ।
items.say: दादी जी एक छोटे गाँव से हैं ।
items.en: Grandmother[0] is[6] from[5] a[2] small[3] village[4].
wrong: छोटा is the direct form. Before से, गाँव is oblique and so is its adjective.
छोटी is feminine. The adjective agrees with गाँव, not with grandmother.
items.why: The adjective agrees with its own noun, गाँव, which is oblique before से.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are new rugs in the small rooms.”
items.say: छोटे कमरों में नई दरियाँ हैं ।
items.en: There are[5] new[3] rugs[4] in[2] the small[0] rooms[1].
wrong: Adjectives never take -õ. Their -e form serves for the oblique singular and plural.
items.why: In the oblique plural, the noun takes -õ but the adjective only -e.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who is in your room? (to तुम)”
items.en: Who[3] is[4] in[2] your[0] room[1]? (to तुम)
wrong: तुम्हारा is the direct form. कमरे is oblique, so the possessive takes -e.
तुम्हारी is feminine, but कमरा is masculine.
items.why: तुम्हारा works like an -ā adjective.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are four daughters in my family.”
items.say: मेरे परिवार में चार बेटियाँ हैं ।
items.en: There are[5] four[3] daughters[4] in[2] my[0] family[1].
wrong: मेरी would agree with बेटियाँ, but the possessive goes with परिवार.
मेरा is the direct form. परिवार is oblique before में.
items.why: मेरा agrees with परिवार, masculine and oblique here.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There is a picture on that white wall.”
items.hi: उस ___ दीवार पर एक तस्वीर है ।
items.say: उस सफ़ेद दीवार पर एक तस्वीर है ।
items.en: There is[6] a[4] picture[5] on[3] that[0] white[1] wall[2].
wrong: सफ़ेद does not end in -ā, so it never changes.
सफ़ेद never changes, so this is not a real form.
items.why: Adjectives that do not end in -ā never change, in the oblique too.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where is your bicycle? (to तुम)”
items.en: Where[2] is[3] your[0] bicycle[1]? (to तुम)
wrong: तुम्हारा is masculine, but साइकिल is feminine.
-e is for masculine nouns, oblique or plural. साइकिल is feminine.
items.why: The possessive agrees with the thing possessed, साइकिल.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Where are my clothes?”
items.en: Where[2] are[3] my[0] clothes[1]?
wrong: मेरा is singular, but कपड़े is plural.
मेरी is feminine, but कपड़े is masculine.
items.why: Here कपड़े is the subject, in the direct plural, and मेरे agrees with it.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who is in this room?”
items.en: Who[3] is[4] in[2] this[0] room[1]?
wrong: यह is the direct form. Before a noun followed by a postposition it becomes इस.
इन is the oblique plural, but कमरे here is one room.
items.why: यह becomes इस in the oblique singular.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How many people are in those cars?”
items.say: उन गाड़ियों में कितने लोग हैं ?
items.en: {How many}[3] people[4] are[5] in[2] those[0] cars[1]?
wrong: वे is the direct form. Before an oblique noun it becomes उन.
उस is singular, but गाड़ियों is plural.
items.why: वे becomes उन in the oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Which room is your book in?”
items.say: तुम्हारी किताब किस कमरे में है ?
items.en: Which[2] room[3] is[5] your[0] book[1] in[4]?
wrong: कौन is the direct form. Before a noun and a postposition it becomes किस.
किन is plural, but the question asks about one room.
items.why: कौन and क्या both become किस in the oblique singular.

items.q: Fill the gap: “from me”
items.en: from[1] me[0]
wrong: मैं is the direct form, only for the subject. Before a postposition it becomes मुझ.
मेरा means “my”. After a postposition you need the pronoun itself, मुझ.
items.why: मैं becomes मुझ before a postposition.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What is in that?”
items.en: What[2] is[3] in[1] that[0]?
wrong: वह is the direct form. Before में it becomes उस.
उन is the oblique plural, “in those”.
items.why: वह becomes उस in the oblique singular.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Which rooms are there fans in?”
items.en: Which[0] rooms[1] {are there}[4] fans[3] in[2]?
wrong: किस is singular, but कमरों is plural.
items.why: कौन and क्या become किन in the oblique plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “There are books in these cupboards.”
items.en: There are[4] books[3] in[2] these[0] cupboards[1].
wrong: ये is the direct form. Before an oblique noun it becomes इन.
इस is singular, but अलमारियों is plural.
items.why: ये becomes इन in the oblique.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who are you angry with?”
items.en: Who[1] are[4] you[0] angry[3] with[2]?
wrong: कौन is the direct form. Before से it becomes किस.
क्या is a direct form, and it asks about things, not people.
items.why: कौन becomes किस before a postposition.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Are you angry with me?”
items.say: क्या आप मुझ से नाराज़ हैं ?
items.en: Are[5] you[1] angry[4] with[3] me[2]?
wrong: मैं is only for the subject. Before से it becomes मुझ.
मेरे means “my”. After से you need the pronoun itself, मुझ.
items.why: मैं becomes मुझ before a postposition.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Sangeeta is angry with them.”
items.en: Sangeeta[0] is[4] angry[3] with[2] them[1].
wrong: वे is the direct form, only for the subject. Before से it becomes उन.
items.why: वे becomes उन before a postposition.

items.en: There are[3] clothes[2] in[1] the cupboard[0].
wrong: पर means “on”. Inside a cupboard is में.
है is singular, but कपड़े is plural.
items.order: For “there is/are …”, the place comes first and the thing after it: अलमारी में कपड़े हैं.

items.en: The clothes[0] are[3] in[2] the cupboard[1].
wrong: अलमारियों is the oblique plural, “cupboards”. There is one cupboard.
कपड़ा is singular, but the English says clothes.
items.order: To say where known things are (“the clothes”), they come first and the place follows. Place-first would mean “there are clothes…”.

items.en: Where[2] is[3] your[0] room[1]?
wrong: Here कमरा is the subject, so it is direct singular and so is its possessive: तुम्हारा.
हो goes with the subject तुम. The subject here is कमरा.

items.en: There are[5] four[3] chairs[4] in[2] this[0] room[1].
wrong: यह is the direct form. Before a noun with a postposition it becomes इस.
कमरा is direct. Before में it is oblique: कमरे.

items.en: Kamala[0] is[4] in[3] the small[1] kitchen[2].
wrong: An -ā adjective before an oblique noun takes -e.
हैं is plural or honorific. Kamala spoken of plainly takes है.

items.en: My[0] wife[1] is[4] from[3] London[2].
wrong: मेरा is masculine, but पत्नी is feminine.

items.en: What[3] is[4] in[2] those[0] drawers[1]?
wrong: वे is the direct form. Before an oblique noun it becomes उन.
दराज़ें is the direct plural. Before में the oblique plural is needed.

items.en: Grandmother[0] is[4] at[3] home[2].
wrong: A respected grandmother (दादी जी) takes the honorific plural हैं.
से means “from”. “At home” is घर पर.

items.en: There are[5] {lots of}[3] books[4] on[2] the black[0] tables[1].
wrong: मेज़ें is the direct plural. Before पर the oblique plural is needed.
बहुत-सारा agrees with किताबें, which is feminine.

items.en: Is[6] there a bus[5] from[2] here[1] to[4] Delhi[3]?
wrong: पर means “on” a surface, or “at” a place or time (घर पर “at home”, समय पर “on time”). “As far as” is तक.

items.en: Who[3] is[4] in[2] that[0] car[1]?
wrong: वह is the direct form. Before a noun with a postposition it becomes उस.

items.en: Perhaps[0] Father[1] is[5] in[4] the garden[3].
wrong: बग़ीचा is direct. Before में it is oblique: बग़ीचे.
A respected father (पिता जी) takes the honorific plural हैं.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: There is a bird at the window.
wrong: The bird is at the window.
That would be चिड़िया खिड़की पर है. With the place first, the sense is “there is …”.
There are two birds at the window.
एक means “one”. Two would be दो चिड़ियाँ.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: The bird is at the window.
wrong: There is a bird at the window.
That would put the place first: खिड़की पर चिड़िया है.
There is no कहाँ and no question mark. This is the answer to that question.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: वे लोग सुबह से यहाँ हैं ।
items.a: Those people have been here since the morning.
wrong: Those people are here until the morning.
“Until” is तक. से with a time means “since”.
That would be वे लोग यहाँ से हैं. Here से follows सुबह, “since the morning”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मेरा भाई लंदन में है और मेरी बहिन भारत में ।
items.a: My brother is in London and my sister is in India.
wrong: My brother is from London and my sister is from India.
My sister is in London and my brother is in India.
भाई (brother) goes with लंदन, बहिन (sister) with भारत.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: उस घर में सारा सामान पुराना है ।
items.a: All the furniture in that house is old.
wrong: All the furniture in those houses is old.
उस is singular. “Those houses” would be उन घरों में.
All the furniture in this house is new.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: There is no नाराज़ here. किस शहर means “which city”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: रात को यह गाँव बहुत सुन्दर है ।
items.a: This village is very beautiful at night.
wrong: This village is very beautiful until night.
“Until” would be तक. रात को means “at night”.
This village is very beautiful in the morning.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: ख़ैर, शायद वह आज बीमार है ।
items.a: Well, perhaps he is ill today.
wrong: Well, he is certainly ill today.
Well, perhaps he is happy today.

items.q: Which sentence means “There is a newspaper on the chair”?
wrong: This puts the newspaper first: “The newspaper is on the chair”, the answer to “where is the newspaper?”.
This says the chair is on the newspaper. पर follows the word it relates to.
items.why: For “there is …”, the place phrase comes first and the thing after it.

items.q: Which question does this sentence answer?
wrong: That is answered with the place first: कुरसी पर अख़बार है.
कैसा asks what something is like. The answer would describe the paper.
items.why: In an answer, the answer words take the place of the question word: कुरसी पर replaces कहाँ.

items.q: When must a noun be in the oblique case?
wrong: When it is the subject of the verb
A verb subject is always in the direct case.
Plural subjects are direct too. Only a following postposition makes a noun oblique.
items.why: Any noun, pronoun or adjective before a postposition is oblique, even when its form does not change.

items.q: Which pronouns keep the same form before a postposition?
wrong: These change: उस, उन, and किस or किन.
items.why: हम, तुम and आप are the same in the direct and oblique cases.

items.q: किस is the oblique singular of…
wrong: क्या also becomes किस before a postposition.
items.why: किस (singular) and किन (plural) are the oblique forms of both कौन and क्या.

items.q: Another correct way to write मुझ से is…
wrong: मैं is the direct form, only for the subject.
मेरा means “my”. After a postposition you need the pronoun itself.
items.why: A postposition after a pronoun may be written separately or joined to it as one word.

items.q: In मेज़ पर, which case is मेज़ in?
items.a: Oblique, because a postposition follows it
wrong: Direct, because its form has not changed
Feminine nouns look the same in the oblique singular, but a following postposition always makes a noun oblique.
The oblique plural would be मेज़ों.
items.why: A noun before a postposition is oblique even when it looks like the direct form.

items.q: Which phrase means “on the white walls”?
wrong: दीवारें is the direct plural. Before पर the noun takes -õ.
सफ़ेद does not end in -ā, so it never changes.
items.why: The noun takes the oblique plural -õ; an adjective not ending in -ā stays the same.
